title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
prompt:
Remove the `n`-th node from the **end** of the list and return the head.

**Example**: `[1,2,3,4,5]`, `n = 2` → `[1,2,3,5]`.

One pass with a gap: advance a `fast` pointer `n` nodes ahead, then move both until fast reaches the end — `slow` now sits just before the target.
hints: A dummy node before the head removes the special case of deleting the first node.
Move `fast` n steps ahead of `slow`, then advance both until `fast.next == null`.
`slow` is now right before the node to delete: `slow.next = slow.next.next`.

solution.explanation: O(n), single pass. The fixed n-node gap means when fast hits the last node, slow is exactly n+1 from the end — i.e. just before the target. Returning `dummy.next` handles the case where the head itself is removed.
